supersedes_namespace: D-RC75-NN and D-RC74-NN are the prior registers and remain authoritative for their own releases. Every D-RC84 entry cites the plan's F/E identifier where one exists so the two registers can be reconciled without renumbering history.

defects.title: A historical OPEN receipt authorizes unlimited local rewrites, including after the epoch closed
defects.detail: The fence receipt is verified locally by MigrateLegacySuffix and never checked against the witness. There is no local record of permit consumption: the only durable consumption check is the operator grant nonce, which is scoped to the grant, not to the fence or the target. The same signed OPEN receipt therefore rewrites any number of distinct targets, and continues to do so after the witness has recorded CLOSED and resumed admitting submissions.
evidence: internal/witness/migration.go:842 verifyFence is a purely local check
internal/witness/migration.go:1030 verifyFence is called once, before BeginTx at :1056
internal/witness/migration.go:1045 the only durable consumption check is the grant nonce
probe: stale OPEN receipt rewrote seq 2 after the witness closed the epoch (rehashed=1, journal=2)
defects.plan_understates: The plan describes F1 as authority surviving after a terminal state. The reachable defect is broader: authority is unbounded within the epoch and across targets.

defects.title: The witness aborts an epoch over a locally committed rewrite, releasing custody over a rewritten suffix
defects.detail: AbortFence refuses only when the custody head moved. A local rewrite never moves the witness head, so the guard is unreachable through any supported path: Submit refuses while the epoch is open, and INSERT INTO custody_log exists only in Ledger.Submit. The only guard is custodyctl's JournalSince count, performed client-side outside any transaction before the abort RPC.
evidence: internal/witness/fence.go:556 head-unchanged guard
internal/witness/fence.go:242 the barrier makes head movement inside an epoch unreachable
internal/witness/ledger.go:323 the only custody_log insert
cmd/custodyctl/main.go:753 JournalSince timestamp count before the RPC
probe: fc.Abort succeeded over a committed rewrite; witness state ABORTED, no active fence
defects.false_confidence: TestFenceAbortRefusedAfterCustodyAdvanced covers a condition the barrier makes unreachable and must be annotated as such.

defects.title: The signer epoch allocator is non-atomic; concurrent rotations share epoch numbers
defects.detail: AdvanceSignerEpoch reads the epoch and writes epoch+1 in two separate autocommit statements with no transaction. Concurrent rotations collide, so custody_log.signer_epoch no longer identifies a key generation. Handle also reads the signer once and the epoch later from a second query, so a rotation in between durably records the new epoch against a row signed by the old key.
evidence: internal/witness/ledger.go:131 AdvanceSignerEpoch read-then-write outside a transaction
internal/witness/service.go:73 signer snapshot at entry, epoch read at :81/:153
probe: 20 concurrent rotations produced 6 distinct epochs and a final durable epoch of 5
defects.plan_understates: The plan's test says many concurrent rotations without asserting that distinct epochs equal rotations.

defects.title: Retired keys still authorize fresh fence, checkpoint and operator-grant authority
defects.detail: VerifyFenceReceipt, VerifyFenceRequest, VerifyCheckpoint and VerifyOperatorGrant all resolve through ResolveAny, which ignores ValidFromIndex/ValidUntilIndex entirely. A key whose window has closed can mint a fresh OPEN receipt, open a new fence, sign the checkpoint that picks the fence base, and issue a new operator grant. VerifyFenceReceipt also never checks SignerEpoch against the key window.
evidence: internal/custody/trust.go:222 ResolveAny ignores the validity window
internal/witness/fence.go:178 kernel request resolves ResolveAny
internal/witness/fence.go:271 fence receipt resolves ResolveAny
internal/witness/witness.go:211 checkpoint resolves ResolveAny
internal/witness/operator_auth.go:176 grant issuer resolves ResolveAny
defects.plan_understates: The plan names fence and trust.go but not VerifyCheckpoint or VerifyOperatorGrant, both of which grant fresh authority today.
defects.residual: A detached operator grant carries no sequence index, so the trust window cannot be applied to it. Closing that needs a signer-epoch window in the trust file; it is folded into the recovery-grant work (D-RC84-06/PR-03).

defects.title: Terminal reply is not bound: finish() accepts a non-terminal state and sources the grant from the untrusted receipt
defects.detail: FenceClient.finish verifies the receipt signature but not the terminal state, the result digest, or the configured grant. It builds the request with GrantDigest taken from the caller-supplied receipt rather than the client's own grant, so End/Abort act under whatever grant the receipt names. accept() performs this check for OPEN; finish() does not.
evidence: internal/witness/fence.go:720 finish builds req.GrantDigest from fence.GrantDigest
internal/witness/fence.go:740 finish verifies only the signature
internal/witness/fence.go:657 accept checks the configured grant; finish does not
defects.severity_note: Downgraded from the plan's P0. A correct witness never returns a non-terminal receipt for End, so the terminal-state gap is robustness against a misbehaving witness. The grant-sourcing defect is reachable today and is the reason this stays P1.

defects.title: An expired grant strands an open epoch; there is no recovery grant type
defects.detail: Resume re-verifies the initiating grant against time.Now() on every call, and PendingFenceIntent filters on grant_digest, so a replacement grant cannot even find the epoch. No recovery authorization type exists. Note that the witness itself does not verify any grant: FenceClient.Abort needs only the kernel-relay key, so the stranding is enforced by the CLI's grant policy rather than by the custodian.
evidence: internal/witness/migration.go:1033 Authorization.verify with time.Now()
internal/witness/fence.go:803 PendingFenceIntent filters grant_digest
cmd/custodyctl/main.go:671 resume skips nonce consumption but not grant verification
defects.red_test_status: requires the Phase 2 recovery API; recorded as a red test in the PR-03 commit that introduces it, not in PR-00
defects.resolution_note: Recovery is a separate repair-authority grant bound to the fence, epoch, transaction, original grant digest, base and the observed local state; the CLI resolves by -fence so a replacement authorization does not need the expired digest to find the epoch.

defects.title: Abort has no enforceable no-commit proof and no local permit-revocation ordering
defects.detail: The witness cannot inspect the local database, so 'no local commit occurred' is a kernel attestation, not a verified fact. The plan states this as an invariant while conceding the equivalent limit for finalize. A resumed kernel can also commit between the recovery inspection and the abort RPC unless the permit is durably revoked locally first.
evidence: plan section C3 concedes the trust boundary for finalize only
plan section D5 derives an authenticated abort from local state without a revocation step
defects.resolution: Demote I-05 to a trust assumption plus a mandatory durable local permit revocation that precedes every abort RPC.
defects.resolution_note: I-05 restated: the abort is preceded by a durable local RevokePermit, and the no-commit claim stays kernel-attested. The witness still cannot inspect the remote database.

defects.title: Custody release requires only the kernel-relay key; the operator grant is never verified at the witness
defects.detail: CloseFence and AbortFence compare req.GrantDigest to the recorded digest. They never verify that the caller holds a signed grant for that digest. Any holder of the kernel-relay key can therefore close or abort any epoch by copying the digest out of the fence receipt, which makes the operator grant decorative at the custodian.
evidence: internal/witness/fence.go:500 grant digest equality only
internal/witness/fence.go:547 grant digest equality only

defects.title: The submission barrier and every transition are positive-state; adding v2 states silently widens them
defects.detail: activeFenceFrom filters state = OPEN. CloseFence and AbortFence switch on CLOSED and ABORTED and fall through for anything else. Introducing PREPARED, FINALIZING or RECOVERY_REQUIRED without changing all three admits submissions during the prepared interval and lets Close succeed while a migration is prepared.
evidence: internal/witness/fence.go:383 state = OPEN
internal/witness/fence.go:503 switch falls through for unknown states
internal/witness/fence.go:550 switch falls through for unknown states
defects.resolution: Barrier becomes state NOT IN (CLOSED, ABORTED); every transition becomes an exhaustive switch with a default refusal; a table test enumerates all declared states.

defects.title: The local fence intent silently ignores a conflicting base and accumulates phantom OPEN epochs
defects.detail: RecordFenceIntent uses ON CONFLICT(fence_id) DO NOTHING, so re-recording the same fence identity with different commitments is ignored instead of refused. openMigrationEpoch inserts a new intent on every stale-base retry and never retires the abandoned ones, and there is no uniqueness constraint on nonterminal epochs.
evidence: internal/witness/fence.go:784 ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING
cmd/custodyctl/main.go:971 a new intent per stale-base attempt
internal/witness/fence.go:753 no unique index on nonterminal state

defects.title: Crash between witness close and CompleteFenceIntent leaves an unrecoverable local/witness disagreement
defects.detail: The local intent stays OPEN while the witness is CLOSED. Reenter fails with ErrFenceState, Plan recomputes the same fence identity because the grant and base are unchanged, and OpenFence refuses a CLOSED fence. Re-enter, open and abort are all refused, and no supported CLI path reconciles the local record.
evidence: cmd/custodyctl/main.go:924 CompleteFenceIntent after End
internal/witness/fence.go:433 OpenFence refuses a non-OPEN existing fence
internal/witness/fence.go:131 FenceIDFor is deterministic on grant and base
defects.resolution_note: PlanRecovery derives COMPLETE when the witness already closed and the local journal records the commit.

defects.title: fence abort relies on a client-side timestamp count outside any transaction
defects.detail: JournalSince compares created_at strings against the fence intent's opened_at and is read before the abort RPC with no transaction spanning the two. A concurrent migrate can commit in that window. The check is also the only thing standing between an operator and the defect in D-RC84-02.
evidence: internal/witness/migration.go:1549 JournalSince
cmd/custodyctl/main.go:753 call site before fc.Abort
defects.resolution: Superseded by the witness-side prepared/committing guard; retain as a defence-in-depth report only.
defects.resolution_note: The witness-side guard is now authoritative; JournalSince remains a defence-in-depth report only.

defects.title: The qualification matrix uses PARTIAL outside the declared status enum
defects.detail: qualification-matrix.json declares PASS/FAIL/NOT_RUN/BLOCKED in the release record, but gate G0-source-identity carries status PARTIAL. A verifier that only allows the declared enum would reject the baseline; one that allows PARTIAL silently accepts an undeclared status.
evidence: qualification/rc8.3-integrity/qualification-matrix.json:21
release-out/GO-NO-GO.md states gate statuses are only PASS / FAIL / NOT_RUN / BLOCKED
defects.resolution_note: The strict validator rejects PARTIAL as an undeclared status. Applied to the RC8.3 matrix it reports 40 findings, not one: most PASS lanes carry no evidence path and several carry no command, so the matrix could not have supported a release decision even after the enum was fixed.

defects.title: The detached evidence bundle has no verifier that runs from shipped files only
defects.detail: cleanroom-verify.sh builds and vets the tree but is executed on the same host under the same operator, and it does not assert that every declared gate belongs to the candidate digest. There is no negative test that a bundle missing a referenced log, carrying a foreign-commit log, or containing an unallowlisted status fails.
evidence: release-out/logs/cleanroom.log
qualification/rc8.3-integrity/tools/verify-evidence-bundle.py
defects.resolution_note: The bundle verifier proves every shipped file is listed and matches, from the bundle alone. Applied to release-out it finds four unaccounted bytes: GO-NO-GO.md, RELEASE-RECORD.json, release-root/key-id.txt and release-root/release-root.pub are shipped but absent from SHA256SUMS.

defects.detail: The doc comment says the check runs before any mutation and again inside the write transaction. grep finds exactly one call site, before BeginTx. A false safety claim in the code is how the next reader concludes the race is already closed.

defects.title: The v2 transaction model contradicts the shipped batch epoch granularity
defects.detail: One epoch currently covers N rewrites of N targets with one close digest. A per-target transaction identity changes the CLI paging loop, adds two RPCs per row inside the frozen window, and changes the close-digest semantics. The plan does not scope this.
